claims.claim: The Cross is the unique configuration satisfying all five conditions of perfect repair (justice, mercy, freedom, record, and restoration) simultaneously.
claims.plain_english: There is only one way to fix everything that's broken without violating justice, mercy, freedom, or truth — and that way is the Cross.
claims.evidence_given: Lean 4 formal proof: JusticeMercyOperator.lean theorem cross_is_unique_solution (Thm 125) — exhaustive case elimination shows any configuration meeting all five conditions is identical to the Cross.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a different configuration (e.g., offender pays, debt waived, coerced third party, shared cost) could satisfy all five conditions simultaneously, the uniqueness claim would be false.

claims.claim: Corrupted systems cannot self-repair using only corrupted resources; external conversion is required.
claims.plain_english: If something is broken from the inside, it can't fix itself — help has to come from outside.
claims.evidence_given: PolarityDiscipline.lean and SignConversionDiscipline.lean: destructive signs cannot self-redeem through ordinary multiplication; burden coupling shows two negatives stay negative; only external Christic conversion flips a negative burden to positive.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a corrupted system could produce a positive outcome using only its own corrupted resources (e.g., self-improvement achieving moral conversion), the claim would be false.

claims.claim: Good is ontologically prior to evil — evil is parasitic on prior good.
claims.plain_english: Evil can't exist on its own; it only makes sense as a corruption of something good that came first.
claims.evidence_given: Sign arithmetic enforces asymmetry: positive is generative, negative is parasitic. Incoherent records not retained; negative states require prior positive substrate to deviate from. Formal model in PolarityDiscipline.lean and SignConversionDiscipline.lean.
claims.what_would_break_it: If evil could exist independently without borrowing from good (e.g., a dualist framework where evil is co-eternal and self-sufficient), the claim would be false.

claims.claim: The Maxwell/Trinity isomorphism holds: quaternion electromagnetics is structurally isomorphic to the relational Trinity under a five-condition structural specification.
claims.plain_english: The math that describes electricity and magnetism has the same shape as the Christian doctrine of the Trinity — and this isn't a coincidence you can fake.
claims.evidence_given: MaxwellTrinity.lean: 24 theorems. Quaternion EM and relational Trinity both pass all 5 ValidTriadic conditions. TriadicIso is proved. Five false positives (Heaviside EM, Modalism, static single-field EM, arbitrary 3-part system, relabeled role system) are all formally rejected. Each guard is load-bearing.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a false positive (e.g., Heaviside EM or Modalism) could pass all five conditions and the TriadicIso, the isomorphism claim would be false.

claims.claim: Coherence requires a prior, stable, truth-bearing, generative, and authoritative standard — the God-shape.
claims.plain_english: For anything to make sense, there has to be a standard of truth that isn't broken itself — and that standard looks like God.
claims.evidence_given: Lane 1 argument: coherence functional defined; zero-factor collapse proved in Core.lean; self-grounding substrate defined; missing source/relation/command forces bridge score to zero. The naming step (Q7) is not formally provable but the shape is argued.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a broken or contingent system could serve as its own final standard of coherence without regress or contradiction, the claim would be false.

claims.claim: The bridge matrix (10-factor signature) is structurally valid: all 10 canonical bridge rows pass signature validation, and semantic swaps (grace↔faith, entropy↔grace, etc.) are correctly rejected.
claims.plain_english: There are exactly 10 key concepts that connect physics and theology, and swapping any two of them breaks the pattern — the math catches the mistake.
claims.evidence_given: BridgeMatrix.lean: 21 theorems. All 10 canonical rows valid. Grace↔Faith swap, Entropy↔Grace swap, K↔F swap, C↔R swap all rejected. Product alone is blind to semantic swaps; signature layer catches what arithmetic misses.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a semantic swap (e.g., grace↔faith) could pass both the product and signature validation, the structural validity claim would be false.

claims.claim: The master equation is invariant under the canonical physical-to-spiritual substitution: χ(physical) = χ(spiritual).
claims.plain_english: The same equation that describes how the universe works also describes how the spiritual world works — they're the same formula.
claims.evidence_given: MasterEquationInvariance.lean: 8 theorems. Canonical substitution preserves signatures for all 10 factors. χ(physical) = χ(spiritual) under canonical map. Both product and signature needed — neither alone suffices.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the canonical substitution did not preserve the master equation (i.e., χ(physical) ≠ χ(spiritual)), the invariance claim would be false.

claims.claim: The Cross is the unique solution to the justice/mercy convergence problem — any configuration satisfying all five conditions is identical to the Cross.
claims.plain_english: There is exactly one way to be perfectly just and perfectly merciful at the same time, and that way is the Cross.
claims.evidence_given: JusticeMercyOperator.lean: 14 theorems. Existence AND uniqueness proved by exhaustive case elimination. Justice and Mercy share 4 components, differ in exactly one coordinate: who pays the cost. Cross satisfies all 5 conditions; every alternative fails at least one.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a configuration other than the Cross could satisfy all five conditions (proportionality, impartiality, truth-naming, victim-restoration, and cost-bearer), the uniqueness claim would be false.

claims.claim: The resurrection is not repair — it is mission return: substrate identity is preserved through incarnation, death, and resurrection, and the post-resurrection state is richer than the pre-incarnate state.
claims.plain_english: The resurrection isn't just fixing what was broken — it's completing a mission, and the result is better than the starting point.
claims.evidence_given: MissionReturnOperator.lean: 13 theorems. Substrate identity preserved through incarnation, cross, and resurrection. Resolution drops from infinite to finite (incarnation) then returns to infinite (resurrection). Entropy and death contact records carried. Post-resurrection ≠ pre-incarnate: it is richer.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the resurrection were merely a return to the pre-incarnate state (a reset) or if substrate identity were lost, the claim would be false.

claims.claim: The Lean 4 corpus proves internal structural consistency: 287 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorry, 0 admit — but it does not prove that the formal models faithfully represent real physics and theology.
claims.plain_english: The computer checked every step of the logic and found no errors, but that doesn't mean the math matches the real world — that's a separate question.
claims.evidence_given: The entire corpus: 287 named theorems across 16 Lean files, all compiling with zero sorry/admit/axioms. The overclaim guard runs on every theorem, explicitly stating what each proves and does not prove. SPEC-01 through SPEC-05 name the limits.
claims.what_would_break_it: If any theorem failed to compile (i.e., contained a sorry, admit, or axiom), the consistency claim would be false. If the formal models were shown to be unfaithful abstractions of the real domains, the relevance claim would be weakened.
